pathway.title: Newmark Group, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is moderate but has risen, and the measure matters. Net debt to reported EBITDA moved from 1.07x at FY2025 to 1.38x at 2026-09-30, or 1.41x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-10-28, against 1.40x at FY2024, while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA grew 10.84%; on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the ratio is 1.00x, and total debt to reported EBITDA is 1.91x. The revolver draw rose alongside capital returns and investment, so leverage is a policy outcome rather than a result of falling earnings. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C31

Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main support for the credit. Undrawn revolver capacity is USD 620 million, no corporate debt matures before 2029 and the revolver runs to 2030. The filings state covenant compliance but print no debt covenant level; the one capital test with a printed margin is Fannie Mae's net worth requirement, where the margin was USD 351.0 million at 2026-09-30, down from USD 386.7 million at year-end 2025, so the headroom that would make the liquidity usable under stress is established for that test alone. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 112; calculation C8; calculation C33; calculation C44

Market access is adequate but sits at the lowest investment-grade step. Fitch and S&P both rate the company BBB- with stable outlooks, S&P having raised its rating from BB+ on 2026-09-16, and the quarterly report says the rate on the senior notes due 2029 may rise by up to 2% after a downgrade; at that maximum the extra interest is USD 12.00 million a year and cover falls from 8.17x to 6.73x. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 116; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C42; calculation C43; calculation C5

Revenue is diversified and about two-fifths recurring, but the transaction lines are slowing at the margin and management has lowered its outlook. Management services and servicing are 39.57% of nine-month revenue and grew 18.30% in the third quarter, and leasing grew 26.49%, but capital markets revenue fell 4.36% in the quarter although it is still 14.55% higher over the nine months, while the ten-year Treasury yield rose about 113 bp in the quarter to 5.3%; the midpoint of the 2026 revenue outlook was cut by 1.96% and that of the adjusted EBITDA outlook by 4.00% because the timing of deal closings is uncertain. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 96–97; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 8; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C10; calculation C9; calculation C39; calculation C23; calculation C35; calculation C14; calculation C15

Margins look resilient because much of the cost base is variable. Compensation and employee benefits are 59.12% of FY2025 revenue and producers earn a substantial portion or all of their pay from production, so costs fall with commissions; the last-twelve-month reported EBITDA margin is 12.39% against 12.32% at FY2024, and the issuer's adjusted margin is 17.25%. Depreciation, lease costs and cash interest do not flex, so a sustained fall in deal volume would compress margin faster than revenue. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C20; calculation C28; calculation C29

Financial policy is the weakest dimension: capital returns are running ahead of free cash flow and are tilted toward insiders. Shareholder returns were 1.39x free cash flow excluding loan activity in the nine months against 1.34x a year earlier, so the gap is persistent and not new, net revolver borrowing was 0.97x of share repurchases, 98.48% of third-quarter repurchases came from the chief executive and his foundation, and the quarterly dividend doubled to USD 0.06 per share, so creditors are competing with equity for cash while the revolver is drawn. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C30; calculation C62; calculation C63; calculation C19; calculation C48; calculation C25; calculation C36

Governance adds risk beyond the numbers. Mr. Brandon Lutnick controls 58.6% of the vote through Cantor and CFGM, Cantor holds 20.83% of the senior notes, the chief executive is contracted as chief executive only through 2026-12-31 with no successor named, and the company is a controlled company that could drop board independence requirements, though it has not done so; the Audit Committee is the stated check on related-party dealing. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C37; calculation C24

The lending business adds claims outside corporate debt that the headline leverage omits. Warehouse facilities fund 99.02% of loans held for sale and are recourse only to a subsidiary, so they are excluded from corporate debt, but total debt including them is 2.49x the corporate figure; separately, Newmark shares losses on Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac loans, with a stated maximum potential loss of about USD 12.1 billion against a risk-sharing liability equal to 0.29% of it, so the exposure is small on expected loss and very large on a maximum basis. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C34; calculation C45; calculation C47

runs.text: Newmark is an average credit with a stable bias: its strengths are balance-sheet and revenue-mix qualities that protect debt service, and its weaknesses are choices by owners and management and a deal market that has turned less supportive. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C8

Liquidity is the first strength: USD 620 million of undrawn revolver, a first corporate maturity in 2029 and BBB- ratings at Fitch and S&P mean refinancing is not a near-term pressure, so stress would show in leverage and ratings before it shows in cash. Moderate leverage is the second: 1.38x on reported EBITDA and cover of 8.17x leave room to absorb a weaker year. Recurring management and servicing revenue, 39.57% of nine-month revenue, is the third because it does not depend on deal closings. A largely commission-based cost base is the fourth because compensation moves with revenue and limits margin loss when deals slow. Earnings momentum is the fifth: last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is 10.84% above FY2025. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 112; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C8; calculation C33; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C23; calculation C31

Capital returns above free cash flow are the first weakness: shareholder returns were 1.39x free cash flow excluding loan activity and the revolver funded 0.97x of repurchases, so owners are paid from debt capacity. Control by one holder and related-party dealing are the second: 58.6% of the vote sits with Mr. Brandon Lutnick, Cantor holds 20.83% of the senior notes and 98.48% of third-quarter repurchases came from the chief executive and his foundation. Dependence on deal volumes is the third: capital markets revenue fell 4.36% in the third quarter and management lowered its outlook. The chief executive transition is the fourth because the contract as chief executive ends on 2026-12-31 with no successor named. Claims outside corporate debt are the fifth: total debt including warehouse facilities is 2.49x the corporate figure and covenant levels are not printed. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C30; calculation C48; calculation C37; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C9; calculation C34

runs.text: The parent's only public debt issue is the 7.500% senior notes due 2029, issued on 2024-01-12 for USD 600.0 million as general senior unsecured obligations; Cantor bought USD 125.0 million, which is 20.83% of the issue, and still holds it. The revolving credit facility was amended and restated on 2026-04-17, raising it to USD 900.0 million with a maturity of 2030-04-17 and a right to increase to USD 1.1 billion. A repurchase agreement for the Multifamily Bridge Program with a USD 300.0 million facility amount was signed on 2026-08-27, and USD 28.0 million was borrowed under it at 2026-09-30, carried inside other liabilities. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 114; calculation C13

No sponsor transaction, merger or change of control is stated in the sources. Control changed within the family when Mr. Howard Lutnick completed the divestiture of his holdings on 2025-10-06, and four small cash acquisitions were completed in 2026 for USD 34.6 million in total. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C18

The quarterly and annual reports state only that Newmark was in compliance with all financial covenants at the balance-sheet dates, and the 2025 annual report names minimum interest coverage and maximum leverage tests only for the former delayed draw term loan, which it describes as consistent with the credit facility then in place. The annual report also names GSE and HUD eligibility criteria, including minimum net worth and operational liquidity, without printing their levels. Headroom is not calculable, and Fundamental credit can report management's compliance statement only; inferring levels from the issuer's net leverage figure would be unsupported.

The release defines net debt as total corporate debt excluding the GSE warehouse facilities, net of cash or liquidity, and net leverage as that net debt over trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA. The issuer's net leverage therefore rests on corporate debt only and on adjusted EBITDA, so it will not agree with a ratio built on reported EBITDA or on debt that includes the warehouse lines, and each ratio must be labelled; whether the warehouse lines count as debt is a perimeter decision for the Financial foundation, not a source question. Reported EBITDA has to be built from statement lines.

fields.value: Financial foundation for Newmark Group, Inc. (issuer nmrk-1690680), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, derived last-twelve-month figures, debt, liquidity, leverage and cover from the eight supplied filings and releases. Upstream source readiness is supplied; no market, rating agency or legal documents are in scope.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Newmark's corporate debt is moderate against reported earnings, with net leverage of 1.38x on reported EBITDA and 1.00x on the issuer's adjusted figure, so the reported measure is the prudent basis for sizing credit risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover on reported EBITDA is 8.17x, undrawn revolver capacity is USD 620.0 million, and the nearest corporate maturity is 2029. Reported EBITDA is derived because the filings state none, and it is far below the issuer's adjusted measure because it carries equity-based compensation as a cost and counts non-cash servicing-right gains as revenue. The third-quarter release and quarterly report print different nine-month cash-flow totals, so the quarterly report is used. The warehouse facilities are excluded from debt as matched funding of loans held for sale; with them, total debt would be much higher.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Corporate debt at carrying value rose from USD 671.746 million at year-end 2025 to USD 877.508 million at 2026-09-30 as the revolver draw went from USD 75.000 million to USD 280.000 million, while cash moved from USD 229.109 million to USD 239.983 million, so net debt rose by USD 194.888 million to USD 637.525 million. Over the same nine months the group spent USD 210.528 million on share repurchases and USD 72.100 million on convertible debt and other contract assets, which is consistent with the extra debt funding capital return and investment. Net debt over last-twelve-month reported EBITDA moved from 1.07x at year-end 2025 to 1.38x, still below 1.40x at year-end 2024, because last-twelve-month reported EBITDA grew from USD 415.305 million to USD 460.319 million. The senior notes principal of USD 600.000 million is unchanged and matures in 2029, and the revolver now matures in 2030, so the added debt sits in the instrument with the later maturity.

fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is the issuer's own framing: on adjusted EBITDA net debt is 1.00x, because the adjusted measure adds back USD 196.892 million of equity-based compensation and partner allocations and removes USD 92.456 million of non-cash servicing-right gains in the nine months. Reported EBITDA treats the compensation as a cost, which is the conservative reading for creditors because the group also spent cash on repurchases and partner distributions of USD 29.209 million in the same period. The view would change if the issuer disclosed how much of the equity-based charge is settled in shares, which would move the right denominator toward the adjusted figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover on reported EBITDA is 8.17x for the last twelve months against 10.50x in FY2024. Cash interest paid rose between FY2024 and FY2025 from USD 32.129 million to USD 56.368 million, and part of it is not corporate-debt interest: corporate debt interest and issue-cost amortization were USD 45.734 million of the USD 53.779 million paid in the nine months, and the sources do not itemise the other USD 8.045 million, which may include warehouse facility interest. Cover on corporate debt alone is therefore better than the printed ratio but cannot be isolated for twelve months from the sources.

fields.value: Business and governance for Newmark Group, Inc. (issuer nmrk-1690680), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, ownership and control, governance, related-party dealing, capital allocation and debt transactions from the supplied annual report, quarterly report and earnings release. Source readiness is supplied; no proxy statement, executed debt document or market data is in scope.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Newmark's business is diversified across service lines and clients, so creditors' main exposure is governance: a Cantor-controlled owner group with 58.6% of the vote, heavy related-party dealing and a chief executive transition at the end of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The largest service line is 39.57% of nine-month 2026 revenue and the top ten clients were 9.1% of FY2025 revenue, so a single client or line is unlikely to impair debt service. The risks that matter to a bondholder come from the controlling holder: Cantor holds USD 125.0 million of the USD 600.0 million senior notes, 98.48% of the shares repurchased in the third quarter came from the chief executive and his foundation, and the Audit Committee is the stated check on related-party deals. The chief executive is contracted as chief executive only through 2026-12-31, and the sources name no successor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control sits with one family through Cantor and is larger than its economic interest, which makes the board and borrowing decisions subject to one group's preferences. Class B shares carry ten votes each, and as of 2026-09-30 Mr. Brandon Lutnick beneficially controlled 58.6% of the vote, while Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P. holds 11.7% of the economics and 56.5% of the voting power and CFGM, Cantor's managing general partner, holds 0.8% of the economics and 1.2% of the voting power. The stated protection for other holders is Audit Committee approval of matters that need it, and a Lutnick family voting agreement that directs the family's votes, so control is stable rather than contestable. Newmark is a controlled company under Nasdaq rules and could opt out of the majority-independent-board requirement, which it has not done to date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Related-party dealing with Cantor is extensive and touches creditors directly, because Cantor is both the controlling holder and a lender and service provider. Cantor holds USD 125.0 million of the USD 600.0 million of senior notes due 2029, which is 20.83% of the issue, and its affiliate CF&Co acts as placement agent and makes a market in the notes; Cantor also supplies administrative services, can borrow from and lend to Newmark under a credit agreement of up to USD 250.0 million with no balance outstanding, and is owed a tax receivable liability. These arrangements are approved by the Audit Committee on terms stated to be no less favorable than third parties, but the agreements themselves were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital returns are heavy and tilted toward insiders, so shareholder distributions are competing with creditors for the same cash. In the third quarter 98.48% of the shares repurchased were bought from the chief executive and his foundation, the quarterly dividend is USD 0.06 per share against USD 0.03 a year earlier, and the repurchase authorization was raised to USD 400.0 million of which USD 189.5 million remained at 2026-09-30. The repurchases were approved by the Audit and Compensation Committees and paid for while the revolver drawings rose, which is the pattern a bondholder should watch.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leadership continuity is the near-term governance risk: the chief executive is contracted as chief executive only through 2026-12-31, after which he becomes Chairman of the operating subsidiary Newmark & Co., and the sources name no successor; the Board retained a leadership advisory firm in July 2025 and says it is assessing long-term options, so a process exists but its outcome is not disclosed. The Board chair is also the chief legal officer, a director is the son of the former executive chairman and now Chief Strategy Officer, and a Chief Operating Officer was appointed in 2025, so management depth exists but the outcome of the succession process is not disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is diversified and part recurring, which is the main offset to governance risk. Management services and servicing is the largest line at 39.57% of nine-month 2026 revenue and grew 19.00%, leasing grew 21.38% and capital markets 14.55%, and the top ten clients were 9.1% of FY2025 revenue; management states a goal of more than USD 2 billion of annual management and servicing revenue by 2029, which is management language, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions are small and cash funded, so they add little integration or leverage risk. The four acquisitions completed in 2026 cost USD 34.6 million in cash in total, against contingent cash consideration of USD 12.2 million recorded for acquisitions since 2022.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a governance concern is procedural and structural, and the company states that it has not relied on any controlled-company exemption from Nasdaq governance standards to date. Related-party transactions need Audit Committee approval and the authorizations state arm's-length price terms, the former executive chairman completed the divestiture of his holdings and holds no voting or dispositive power, revenues are spread over three service lines and many clients, and the quarterly report shows no outstanding balance under the Cantor credit agreement. The view would turn more positive if the proxy materials show a majority of independent directors and an independent chair, if the issuer names a chief executive successor with an orderly handover, and if insider repurchases stop; it would turn more negative if Cantor sold its notes at a discount or the revolver were drawn to fund further insider buybacks. The Board has also had a leadership advisory firm assisting with long-term succession planning since July 2025, which lowers the risk that the end-2026 transition is unplanned. A single Class B voting block can also be an asset to creditors if it is a stable, long-horizon holder, which the sources neither confirm nor rule out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Newmark's fundamental credit profile is average: moderate leverage, strong liquidity and fee revenue spread across service lines support debt service, but capital returns above free cash flow, a lowered outlook and controlling-holder influence leave little room above the lowest investment-grade ratings.

fields.value: Leverage is moderate but has risen, and the measure matters. Net debt to reported EBITDA moved from 1.07x at FY2025 to 1.38x at 2026-09-30, or 1.41x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-10-28, against 1.40x at FY2024, while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA grew 10.84%; on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the ratio is 1.00x, and total debt to reported EBITDA is 1.91x. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is momentum, modest leverage and improving ratings: nine-month revenue grew 18.36%, third-quarter revenue grew 12.71%, last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is 10.84% above FY2025, net leverage on the issuer's own adjusted measure is 1.00x, S&P raised the rating to BBB- on 2026-09-16, and management still expects its best-ever full year. The profile would improve if shareholder returns fell back inside free cash flow and the revolver were repaid, if a chief executive successor were named with an orderly handover, and if the executed credit agreement showed ample covenant headroom. It would weaken if capital markets revenue fell again year on year in the fourth quarter, if net leverage stayed above the FY2024 level of 1.40x after the dividend, if revolver availability fell toward the USD 365 million of 2026-03-31, or if a downgrade triggered the rate increase on the notes.

fields.value: Newmark is an average credit with a stable bias: its strengths are balance-sheet and revenue-mix qualities that protect debt service, and its weaknesses are choices by owners and management and a deal market that has turned less supportive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the first strength: USD 620 million of undrawn revolver, a first corporate maturity in 2029 and BBB- ratings at Fitch and S&P mean refinancing is not a near-term pressure, so stress would show in leverage and ratings before it shows in cash. Moderate leverage is the second: 1.38x on reported EBITDA and cover of 8.17x leave room to absorb a weaker year. Recurring management and servicing revenue, 39.57% of nine-month revenue, is the third because it does not depend on deal closings. A largely commission-based cost base is the fourth because compensation moves with revenue and limits margin loss when deals slow. Earnings momentum is the fifth: last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is 10.84% above FY2025.

Control by one holder and related-party dealing are the second: 58.6% of the vote sits with Mr. Brandon Lutnick, Cantor holds 20.83% of the senior notes and 98.48% of third-quarter repurchases came from the chief executive and his foundation. Dependence on deal volumes is the third: capital markets revenue fell 4.36% in the third quarter and management lowered its outlook. The chief executive transition is the fourth because the contract as chief executive ends on 2026-12-31 with no successor named. Claims outside corporate debt are the fifth: total debt including warehouse facilities is 2.49x the corporate figure and covenant levels are not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Newmark is a commercial real estate adviser and service provider with three revenue lines: management services, servicing fees and other; leasing and other commissions; and capital markets. About two-fifths of nine-month revenue is recurring fee income and the top ten clients were 9.1% of FY2025 revenue, so debt service does not rest on one client or one line. The cost of that breadth is dependence on the transaction lines, which follow deal volumes and interest rates, so cash-flow visibility is good for the fee half of the business and weak for the commission half.

fields.value: One holder controls the vote: Mr. Brandon Lutnick controls 58.6% of it through Cantor and CFGM, Cantor holds 20.83% of the senior notes, and related-party services, lending and note placement run through the same group. Control is stable rather than contestable, which lowers takeover risk but means borrowing, distributions and board makeup follow one group's preferences, and creditor protection rests on Audit Committee approval of related-party matters. No sponsor transaction, merger or change of control is stated in the documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical in its transaction half and sticky in its fee half. Leasing grew 26.49% and management services and servicing grew 18.30% in the third quarter, while capital markets fell 4.36% although it is still 14.55% higher over the nine months, so the commission lines now pull in different directions. Management states a goal of more than USD 2 billion of annual management and servicing revenue by 2029; that is management language, not a forecast, and it would raise the recurring share only if met.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost flexibility is good where it matters. Compensation and employee benefits are 59.12% of FY2025 revenue and follow commission-based revenue, as the third-quarter release attributes the cost increase primarily to higher commission-based revenue, acquired companies and growth investment, so a drop in deal fees is partly met by lower pay. Depreciation, lease costs and cash interest do not flex, and the last-twelve-month reported EBITDA margin of 12.39% is close to the 12.32% of FY2024 even though the adjusted margin is 17.25%, because the reported measure carries equity-based compensation as a cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is high and capital intensity low. Free cash flow excluding loan activity was 72.52% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA against 57.59% in FY2024, after cash interest and taxes, and purchases of fixed assets are 1.53% of last-twelve-month revenue, so little cash is locked in maintenance spending and capital spending is easy to cut. The main recurring use of operating cash is advances to employees and partners to hire and retain producers; loan originations swing reported operating cash flow but are matched by warehouse funding, so the swing is timing and not a drain on corporate cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is the force that matters most to margins and market position. The annual report describes an industry that is fragmented and competitive, names larger rivals such as CBRE, Jones Lang LaSalle and Cushman & Wakefield, and says some competitors are substantially larger than Newmark; the third-quarter report says Newmark believes it gained share in investment sales, yet its U.S. debt volumes fell about 37% while industry originations rose, which the issuer ties to a strong prior-year comparison. Buyer power is limited by client spread, with the top ten clients at 9.1% of FY2025 revenue and clients increasingly awarding work to full-service firms. Supplier power sits with producers, who earn a substantial portion or all of their pay from production and are retained with advances, so producer departures are a margin and revenue risk. The documents do not discuss new entrants or substitutes, so those forces are not established.

fields.value: The external factors that move credit are economic and regulatory. A ten-year Treasury yield up about 113 bp in the quarter to 5.3%, tied by the issuer to the Middle East conflict and energy prices, raises financing costs and rate volatility for property buyers and offsets the help from narrow credit spreads. Agency programs add a regulatory layer: capital and liquidity requirements for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac lending include the net worth test the issuer calls its most restrictive, and the Fannie Mae loss-sharing exposure rises with agency loan performance. Technology cuts both ways, because artificial intelligence firms drive office leasing demand while the annual report lists their use as a risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit-translated summary is as follows. Strengths are the liquidity profile, moderate leverage, recurring fees and a flexible cost base. Weaknesses are capital returns above free cash flow, controlling-holder influence and a leadership transition. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are an industry estimate of about USD 2.1 trillion of commercial and multifamily mortgage maturities from 2026 to 2028, which supports refinancing and sales activity, and growth of recurring revenue. Threats that could weaken it are sustained high long-term rates that suppress deal volumes, a downgrade that lifts the notes rate, and agency loss-sharing losses in a credit downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The next one to two years turn on the fourth quarter and on the rate path. The revised outlook implies fourth-quarter revenue growth of between -1.40% and 8.54% against the fourth quarter of 2025, with 3.57% at the midpoint, compared with 12.71% in the third quarter, and the fourth quarter has averaged about 30% of annual revenue, so the outlook leaves little cushion if closings slip. Tailwinds are the leasing recovery led by technology demand, growth in servicing fees and the refinancing wave in industry mortgage maturities; headwinds are rate volatility, the issuer's U.S. debt volumes falling about 37% in the third quarter against a strong prior-year comparison, and lower guidance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the question is refinancing. The senior notes due 2029 of USD 600.0 million become current in 2028, the revolver matures in 2030, and the notes carry a rate that rises on a downgrade, so keeping the investment-grade ratings matters more than any single quarter. Management's goal of more than USD 2 billion of recurring management and servicing revenue by 2029 would improve visibility if met, but it is management language and carries no stated probability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is long-term rates that stay near 5.3% through the year-end selling season, so closings slip and the fourth quarter lands at the low end of the revised outlook, which implies fourth-quarter revenue growth of -1.40%. The first operational break is in the transaction lines, leasing and capital markets, while servicing and management fees keep growing. Compensation flexes with commissions, but depreciation, lease costs and cash interest do not, so reported EBITDA falls faster than revenue. As a severity marker chosen by the analyst, not a forecast, take reported EBITDA back at its FY2024 level: net debt at 2026-09-30 would then be 1.89x EBITDA, or 1.92x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-10-28, and interest cover would be 5.98x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity holds in this case. USD 620 million of the revolver is undrawn and no corporate debt matures before 2029, so no refinancing event arises within the scenario. Management has levers: share repurchases and the dividend are discretionary with USD 189.5 million of repurchase authorization still unused, purchases of fixed assets are only 1.53% of revenue, and producer pay flexes. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; the first constraint would be leverage at 1.89x to 1.92x and the investment-grade ratings, where a downgrade lifts the notes rate, and not cash. The scenario would break this view only if repurchases continued at the nine-month pace while earnings fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8; calculation C33; calculation C53; calculation C61; calculation C42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Newmark presents an adequate business profile supported by revenue spread across three service lines, low capital intensity and investment-grade ratings at Fitch and S&P, but credit quality is constrained by capital returns above free cash flow, controlling-holder influence and an earnings base that depends on deal closings in the fourth quarter. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow excluding loan activity converted 72.52% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA and about two-fifths of revenue is recurring. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on keeping the BBB- ratings and on the notes due 2029 being refinanced before they become current. The primary downside path is a weak fourth quarter and a downgrade while the revolver funds distributions. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indenture, the proxy statement, and peer and market data. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: shareholder returns funded by the revolver ahead of a deal-dependent fourth quarter.
